findings.corrective_action: Persist BROADCAST with the transaction hash before waiting for a receipt. Represent timeout as BROADCAST_UNKNOWN, block replacement execution, and reconcile the receipt and wallet state asynchronously before applying cooldown or P&L.

evidence.detail: Lines 198-201 broadcast a transaction and then raise if receipt polling times out. Lines 218-220 catch that exception, discard the known transaction hash, and persist status REJECTED.
Lines 48-54 count only BROADCAST, SUCCESS, SUCCESS_FEE_PENDING, FAILED, and FEE_PENDING toward cooldown/rate limits; REJECTED is excluded.

findings.impact: A transaction that landed after an RPC timeout is treated as never submitted. The same wallet can execute another route on the next cycle, exceeding intended trade frequency/capital exposure while the original trade remains untracked.
findings.root_cause: Broadcast and pre-broadcast failures share one exception handler, and the transaction hash is scoped inside the success path rather than durably recorded immediately after submission.
tests_required: Simulate send success followed by receipt timeout and assert the transaction hash is retained.
Assert uncertain broadcasts consume cooldown/rate-limit capacity.
Assert a later reconciliation updates the same row without submitting a second trade.
findings.title: Receipt uncertainty is recorded as REJECTED and permits duplicate automatic execution

findings.corrective_action: Remove account-specific arming from imports. Implement an explicit authenticated migration command requiring expected environment/deployment identity and current-state confirmation; record migration state transactionally in durable configuration. Fresh installs must default to all LIVE/AUTO gates off.

evidence.detail: Lines 85-92 unconditionally import account-specific LIVE migrations during every real application startup.

Lines 26-49 create Telegram ID 6760898817 if absent and promote it to active MASTER. Lines 51-88 enable AUTO, LIVE, ARMED, SiBot AUTO, and Solana LIVE. The only idempotency control is a marker under the mutable data directory.
Lines 131-165 enable the platform AUTO gate, Polygon LIVE gate, user LIVE settings, and Polygon focus whenever deployment markers are absent.

findings.impact: A disaster recovery, new host, lost marker volume, or data-directory migration can silently recreate privileged identity and real-money execution settings. Repository code, rather than deployment authorization, becomes sufficient to arm LIVE operation.
findings.root_cause: One-time operational actions were embedded in import-time application code and keyed only by local marker files that are not authoritative configuration state.
tests_required: Start with an empty data directory and assert no user is created and all LIVE/AUTO gates remain off.
Restore configuration without marker files and assert operator settings are not changed.
Test an explicit migration command for authorization, idempotency, audit logging, and fail-closed behavior.
findings.title: Fresh or partially restored data directories automatically create a hard-coded MASTER and arm LIVE trading

findings.corrective_action: Move operational ledgers and execution state to SQLite transactions with unique event identifiers. Until then, use one shared lock plus unique temporary files and re-read under lock; use OS-level locking if multiple processes may write.

evidence.detail: Line 142 starts Telegram, power-discovery, and fast-market threads alongside the main loop.
Lines 30-45 read an entire CSV, append, write a shared .tmp name, and replace the destination without a lock.
Lines 96-109 perform the same unlocked read-modify-replace pattern for live_trade_audit.csv.
Lines 41-49 use an unlocked shared temporary filename for the fee ledger.
Lines 10-25 and 41-73 update execution_queue.csv without a process-wide lock.

findings.impact: Concurrent writers can lose rows, overwrite newer settings, raise FileNotFoundError while replacing the same temporary file, or corrupt audit/cooldown evidence. Missing execution rows can subsequently weaken rate limits and accounting reconciliation.
findings.root_cause: Atomic rename protects readers from partial files but does not make a multi-step read-modify-write operation mutually exclusive.
tests_required: Barrier-synchronize multiple writers to each shared ledger and assert all unique rows survive.
Exercise Telegram and execution writers concurrently.
Verify no shared temporary-file collision and no lost cooldown/audit records.
findings.title: Shared CSV read-modify-replace operations are not synchronized across runtime threads

findings.corrective_action: Hash the canonical strategy specification. Return the existing row unchanged when the hash matches; increment version only for a changed specification, preserve lifecycle state, and store versions as immutable rows.

evidence.detail: Lines 194-205 increment version for every registration of an existing strategy and force status='SHADOW' on conflict, without checking whether its specification changed.
Lines 31-66 cache strategy IDs only in process memory, so the first use after each restart invokes register_strategy again.
Lines 28-42 depend on the registered strategy and its evaluated lifecycle state to reduce position sizing.

findings.impact: Every process restart can manufacture a new strategy version despite identical code/specification and transiently revert REWORK, REPLACE, or PROMOTION_CANDIDATE to SHADOW. Trade provenance and lifecycle histories no longer identify actual strategy changes reliably.
findings.root_cause: Registration is implemented as an unconditional version bump/upsert rather than an idempotent create-or-compare operation.
tests_required: Register the same specification across simulated restarts and assert version/status remain unchanged.
Change one parameter and assert exactly one new immutable version is created.
Assert trade provenance references the correct immutable version.
findings.title: Re-registering an unchanged strategy creates phantom versions and resets lifecycle status

findings.corrective_action: Set cancel-in-progress to false and serialize deployments. Make the restricted wrapper transactional with staging, validation, atomic release switching, and rollback; publish attestation for every attempted target.

evidence.detail: Lines 13-15 configure a global deployment concurrency group with cancel-in-progress: true.
Lines 64-84 run the mutable deployment through a self-hosted VPS wrapper. Cancellation can terminate this step before status and attestation complete.
Lines 3-8 allow both main pushes and manual dispatches, making overlapping requests expected.

findings.impact: A second push or dispatch can terminate installation/restart work midway, leaving a partially updated environment or ambiguous running commit while the replacement deployment begins.
findings.root_cause: Cancellation semantics suitable for CI are applied to a state-mutating deployment job.
tests_required: Dispatch two deployments while the first is inside the wrapper and verify strict serialization.
Inject cancellation/failure at each deployment phase and verify rollback to the prior attested commit.
Assert the running commit equals the final successful target.
findings.title: A newer deployment cancels an in-progress VPS deployment

findings.corrective_action: Declare solders in project dependencies or a required runtime extra that startup imports conditionally. Generate deployment requirements from one authoritative dependency definition.

evidence.detail: Lines 10-15 declare requests, python-dotenv, web3, and cryptography but omit solders.
Line 5 separately declares solders>=0.28,<0.29.
Module-level imports require solders.keypair, solders.message, solders.signature, and solders.transaction.
The startup composition imports Solana LIVE modules unconditionally, so a standards-based installation from pyproject metadata fails before CLI startup.

findings.impact: Installing the package with pip/build metadata rather than requirements.txt produces an environment that cannot start the bot, including EVM-only commands because the Solana patch stack is imported globally.
findings.root_cause: Dependency declarations diverged between requirements.txt and pyproject.toml.
tests_required: Build a wheel, install it into an empty environment without requirements.txt, and run python -m learnerbot --help.
Run the module import sweep against the installed wheel.
Verify dependency metadata contains a compatible solders requirement.
findings.title: Published project metadata omits the mandatory Solana runtime dependency

findings.corrective_action: Pin exact package versions and integrity hashes, pin GitHub Actions by commit SHA, separate analysis from write-capable promotion jobs, and pass only the minimum credential to each isolated step.

evidence.detail: Lines 8-11 grant write permissions; lines 51-59 install @openai/codex@latest and @google/gemini-cli@latest at runtime.
Lines 39-48 install unpinned latest AI CLIs; lines 52-57 expose provider and assignment credentials to the workflow.
The workflow installs @openai/codex@latest, supplies OPENAI_API_KEY, and later possesses contents/actions write authority for branch creation, merge, and deployment dispatch.

findings.impact: An upstream package compromise or incompatible release is immediately executed in a credentialed job and can exfiltrate API tokens, manipulate review artifacts, or misuse repository write/dispatch authority.
findings.root_cause: Tool installation prioritizes newest releases over reproducible, integrity-pinned workflow dependencies.
tests_required: Verify all external Actions and npm/pip tools are pinned by immutable version or digest.
Add policy CI rejecting @latest and mutable action tags in privileged workflows.
Confirm analysis jobs run with read-only repository permissions and no unrelated secrets.
findings.title: Privileged AI workflows execute unpinned latest CLI packages with repository credentials

findings.corrective_action: Track bucket largest_loss independently while iterating rows and merge it with the previous window maximum.

evidence.detail: Lines 188-197 aggregate all negative trades in a bucket into gross_loss.
Lines 91-104 pass that aggregate gross_loss to max(previous largest_loss, gross_loss), so multiple smaller losses become one fictitious largest loss.

findings.impact: Risk reports overstate single-trade loss magnitude and may drive incorrect Strategy Lab decisions or operator investigation.
findings.root_cause: The aggregation bucket does not retain the maximum individual negative net value separately from total gross loss.
tests_required: Record two losses of 1 and 2 units in one window and assert gross_loss=3 while largest_loss=2.
Verify incremental updates preserve the maximum across batches.
findings.title: Direct-market Strategy Lab largest loss records aggregate losses instead of the largest individual loss

refusals_or_limits: Report-only review: no files, configuration, capital settings, secrets, wallets, signing material, deployments, or live systems were changed.
The requested commit was verified as checked out exactly and the worktree was clean.

Runtime tests and compile checks could not execute because neither python nor pytest is installed in the supplied environment; both commands failed before repository code ran. Findings therefore rely on deterministic source/control-flow evidence and test inspection.
summary: Found concrete execution-recovery, configuration, concurrency, lifecycle-accounting, deployment, packaging, and CI supply-chain defects. The most serious can cause an already-broadcast EVM trade to be retried, silently arm real-money trading during state restoration, or interrupt an in-progress VPS deployment.
